items.title: Ship the single-player property game
items.notes: The browser game covers token selection, property decisions, end-of-game results, and restart.

items.title: Run the game on the Next.js App Router with TypeScript
items.notes: The application includes pnpm commands for development, type checking, production build, and start.

items.title: Preserve the original Weird Web October URLs
items.notes: The root page and statistics handlers have legacy rewrites under /2025/spooky.

items.title: Persist token unlocks in the browser
items.notes: A finished game can unlock new tokens for future runs in the same browser origin without Supabase.

items.title: Connect shared statistics to Supabase
items.notes: The app can submit and aggregate results through the existing wwo_2025_spooky_game_stats table when configured. A live environment is a separate verification item.

items.title: Document the project and contributor workflow
items.notes: The README links to the guides, agent instructions, and structured roadmap. The first inventory uses its creation date for earlier work without a recorded completion timestamp.

items.title: Check the original event URLs alongside the root routes
items.notes: Verified both production page URLs, the expected API methods, 405 on mismatched methods, and the 503 payloads without Supabase using pnpm test:routes after a production build.

items.title: Distinguish empty, unconfigured, and failed statistics
items.notes: The end-game sidebar distinguishes missing configuration, empty results, and retryable failure. Restart remains available.

items.title: Cover unavailable and empty statistics states
items.notes: Added request-state fixtures, checked missing configuration through production routes, and verified retry to the empty state during a simulated full game.

items.title: Make property decisions faster and explicit
items.notes: Exposed legal Buy, Pass, and Continue controls while preserving passive landing prompts. A vampire can continue when unable to buy but cannot dismiss an affordable purchase. Added action fixtures and verified a full round using fixed rolls in a simulated browser.

items.title: Explain faction rules and surface earned unlocks
items.notes: The picker names each faction and explains its rules and unlock conditions. End-game results tell the player when a new faction is earned.

items.title: Add regression coverage for browser token unlocks
items.notes: Added storage and qualifying-result fixtures. Verified an elf unlock on restart and after a fresh mount on the same simulated browser origin.

items.title: Add a regression check for the local game flow
items.notes: Added a production Chromium fixed-roll suite covering token choice, purchase and pass, special and owned landings, all 20 turns, and restart. It asserts the final cash totals and checks unlocks after reload. The property-action test separately covers an unaffordable vampire landing.

items.title: Make the full game playable on phones and tablets
items.notes: Verified complete rounds in Chromium at 320 × 568, 390 × 844, and 1024 × 768. The compact dock keeps Roll, the turn, current space, and cash within reach. Checks cover horizontal overflow, 44 CSS-pixel tap targets, primary action contrast, and focus restoration. Intro and turn log are expandable.

items.title: Resume an interrupted run in the same browser
items.notes: Added versioned browser-local saves with explicit token and board identifiers. Chromium verifies reload during a pending purchase, then reload after a committed purchase with the same cash and ownership. Start new discards the save, and malformed or unknown versions open normal token selection.

items.title: Export a shareable card from a completed game
items.notes: Added plain-text result copying with a selectable fallback and a downloadable PNG generated in the browser. Chromium verifies the faction, cash and property totals in the copied text, the clipboard fallback, and the PNG header with Supabase disabled.

items.title: Share repeatable challenges using a seeded run
items.notes: Extracted deterministic solo turn rules and added opt-in versioned challenge links with stable token IDs and a saved seed. Chromium verifies two independent browser profiles produce the same result and turn log with identical actions, including after one reloads mid-turn. It also verifies unsupported rules feedback, copying the link, and keeping an existing save when declining a challenge.

items.title: Compare an alternate property decision in Ghost Ledger
items.notes: Recorded rolls and choices in local saves and added the end-game Ghost Ledger. It checks that the original replay matches the reported result, shows cash and owned property names side by side, and stops at the first invalid later action. Chromium verifies both a replay that reaches the final turn and one that stops on turn 17. Comparisons leave the reported result unchanged.

items.title: Resolve shared turns on the server
items.notes: Implemented and verified server-side turn resolution with room-scoped seat authentication, revision checks and idempotent receipts. SQLite persists state and receipts together. The production HTTP test races identical actions and forces a receipt insertion error to verify rollback.

items.title: Let two players join a private match by invite
items.notes: Implemented the Play with a friend entry, one-use invitations, separate browser credentials, editable names and readiness controls. Production HTTP tests verify room isolation. Chromium verifies two profiles joining, readying and retaining the guest seat after reload at 320 CSS pixels.

items.title: Persist and synchronise shared match state
items.notes: Implemented persistent SQLite room, match and receipt state for the single-host pilot. Both Chromium profiles completed the same match and saw the same result, with polling observation latency below three seconds at the 95th percentile on the local test.
